description: Data-only adversarial fixture matrix for local public-tap import. Expected results are explicit per case. No fixture is executed here. The cask_catalog::tap interface is agreed (see design.md section 4: import-tap CLI with --source/--revision/--system/--nix/--out); importer execution happens only in a clean verification sandbox without model credentials. The final normal-mode native reader stage ran on both hosts on 2026-09-29 (20 cases per OS; see docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/normal-reader-summary.json); converter expectations below reflect the backend's final actual converter classification, proven by the seven capture-case regressions (docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/converter-captures.log, 7/7) and the final whole import of the seven real pinned sources on both hosts (docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/results.md section E1). This is stage evidence, not a claim that every case here was whole-imported natively: the installer-script and branch fixture whole-imports and the native two-tree collision import stay explicit limits, and the client-resolution and sandbox-probe cases remain documented-check rows. Normal mode means an explicitly unset HOMEBREW_DEVELOPER environment variable; upstream may still print a developer-command warning, which is not a failure. Internal path loading is explicitly permitted for our staged trusted reader. There is no fixture-runner interface; do not invent a production local-source bypass.
layout: Every independent case gets its own small tree, because a source-wide failure (duplicate token) aborts its whole tree and must not hide other cases. The only cross-tree token sharing is the intentional collision pair (collision-a/collision-b). Tree names map to synthetic source ids in source_id below.

policy.url_policy: Fixtures carry literal local/private destinations only (localhost, 192.168.1.9, 169.254.169.254, [::1]). Redirect and DNS policy belong to backend tests; no fixture can prove redirect handling, so only the documented literal-destination expectation is asserted here. Sandbox denial proofs are not fixtures here: the parent runs controlled native Nix probes and the backend runs the real reader-gate probe with positive controls; a missing control is a failure, never a pass.

expect.notes: Plain GitHub-style release zip. Both targets are supported through actual on_macos/on_linux blocks: app bundle on macOS, a binary from the archive on Linux. No platform support is marked without an OS block.

Raw release binary. The binary source names the download basename (pubtap-raw-binary-0.9.0.bin) with an explicit target rename, so it is a valid generic raw-binary case on both systems via on_macos/on_linux blocks.
macOS-only app bundle in a dmg with the current supported symbol depends_on macos: :sonoma. Linux must be excluded with a platform reason, never guessed.

Actual arch branch (arch arm/intel interpolated into the URL and the sha256 variants), on_macos/on_linux blocks, depends_on macos: :ventura, two language blocks that each return their language code, and name/homepage/desc supplied normally outside the language blocks. The require_relative helper is part of whole-tree identity.

Both variants load cleanly: the cask requires the helper via require_relative and both helper variants define it. The cask file is byte-identical in v1/v2; only the helper VERSION value changes (1.4.0 vs 1.4.1), so the imported version and URL differ AND the whole-tree hash differs. Cached export output must be invalidated by the tree change; the test must not pass merely because a variant failed to load.

harness.documented_check: helper-only invalidation one-off check in tools/public-tap-check/README.md

expect.notes: Artifact list derives from the upstream staging accessor. The importer maps every pkg_error to excluded reason ruby-load-error with bounded detail; for this case the detail must contain staged_path, and that explicit guard detail is what proves the record was excluded for the staging reason, not for an unrelated one. Excluded on both targets; no guessed empty artifact list; no payload download to satisfy it. The tree also holds one valid positive-control cask (pubtap-staging-control, expected eligible): the actual reader fails a whole export when every record fails, so the import must emit the excluded record plus the eligible control record. Both records are part of the expected inventory.

The source rescues the staging error and offers a static fallback, but the reader still fails during source eval, so the importer emits excluded reason ruby-load-error with bounded detail; the detail must contain staged-path-during-source-eval. The refusal flag must stay sticky; the rescue must not create eligibility. The tree also holds one valid positive-control cask (pubtap-staging-rescued-control, expected eligible): the actual reader fails a whole export when every record fails, so the import must emit the excluded record plus the eligible control record. Both records are part of the expected inventory.

Legacy preflight and postflight callback blocks load under the final normal-mode reader (HOMEBREW_DEVELOPER explicitly unset; the upstream developer-command warning may still print and is not a failure). The final actual converter test excludes this record as unsupported-artifact, with a detail naming the callback keys; it is NOT installer-script and NOT ruby-load-error. The deprecated legacy shape is preserved on purpose. The tree also holds one valid positive-control cask (pubtap-flights-control, expected eligible): the actual reader fails a whole export when every record fails, so the import must emit the excluded record plus the eligible control record. Both records are part of the expected inventory. Reader-only success is not converter eligibility.

Structured postflight_steps block with a run stanza using a literal command shape (run "/usr/bin/true", args: []); no staged_path appears in the steps DSL, where it is undefined. Distinct from the legacy callback case: the steps must be captured as structured step data (not a legacy callback), preserved in metadata, and the final actual converter test excludes the record as installer-script. run describes a future command; it is never executed during export.

Installer script stanza with a literal relative executable path (install.sh) and literal args; no staged_path interpolation. Installer scripts are excluded with the installer-script reason by the final actual converter test, never executed. The literal shape keeps the record loadable so the classifier exclusion can be asserted.

Two files with the same basename pubtap-dup.rb in Casks/a and Casks/b, both declaring token pubtap-dup: a genuine duplicate token, not a token/filename mismatch. The refresh must fail the whole (isolated) source and the previous catalog bytes must remain.

Per-record syntax error becomes one excluded entry with reason ruby-load-error and bounded detail; the source continues; diagnostics are bounded. The tree also holds one valid positive-control cask (pubtap-broken-control, expected eligible): the actual reader fails a whole export when every record fails, so the import must emit the excluded record plus the eligible control record. Both records are part of the expected inventory.

Emits exactly output_exhaustion_emit_bytes (fixed, baked in from policy; no environment override can unbound the fixture) then stops; no infinite loop; one isolated tree. Captured diagnostics must be capped at max_captured_output_bytes by the runner WHILE the command runs; result size must be capped; the case passes only if the capture stays within bounds and no hang occurs. Classification may be eligible or excluded; the bound is the assertion.

harness.documented_check: bounded-run pattern in tools/public-tap-check/README.md (timeout plus capped capture); measured stage coverage and limits are recorded in docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/results.md

expect.notes: URL is a literal localhost address, so the destination policy must refuse it without any DNS lookup; the final actual converter test excludes it as unsupported-url. Redirect handling cannot be proven by any fixture; that belongs to backend tests.
URL is a literal RFC1918 address; refused without a lookup and excluded as unsupported-url. Redirect/DNS policy stays in backend tests.
URL is the literal link-local metadata-service address; refused without a lookup and excluded as unsupported-url. Redirect/DNS policy stays in backend tests.
URL is a literal IPv6 loopback address; refused without a lookup and excluded as unsupported-url. Redirect/DNS policy stays in backend tests.

Intentional two-source pair. Both sources publish token editor (eligible in both). Token viewer is excluded in collision-a (the cask source touches the staging accessor, so it fails the reader load; ruby-load-error with a staged-path detail) and eligible in collision-b. Bare editor and bare viewer must both stay ambiguous; the excluded viewer match counts; no ordering precedence; qualified identities resolve only within their source.

harness.documented_check: client commands after import in the clean sandbox; measured stage coverage and limits are recorded in docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/results.md

expect.notes: Acceptance case: one saved source catalog is unreadable or malformed while another saved source has the same bare token. Bare-token resolution must fail for the whole pass. The client must report the failed source. It must not ignore the failed source and select the other source. No fixture file: this is a client-state condition prepared during the run.

harness.documented_check: corrupt one saved catalog, then attempt bare-token install; measured stage coverage and limits are recorded in docs/verification/public-taps-2026-09-29/results.md
